articles.title: Violent clashes between police and protesters in Albania
articles.summary: Police in Albania's capital Tirana have fired tear gas and water cannons onto crowds gathered outside the Ministry of Education where students are among those protesting.
articles.body:
Student protests have continued for a fifth day in Albania's capital Tirana as students gathered outside the Ministry of Education to continue to demonstrate against poor education facilities, rising living costs and alleged government corruption.

The protests quickly turned violent with footage showing protesters throwing molotov cocktails towards police.

In response, riot police have clashed with the protesters, using tear gas and water cannons to disperse them.

The protesters have demanded the resignation of the country's Prime Minister Edi Rama, but he is reported to be resisting demands to step down.

articles.title: Fumaça em Manaus reduz visibilidade e ar atinge nível perigoso | G1
articles.standfirst: Registro foi feito quando Manaus no topo do ranking de cidades com pior qualidade do ar do Brasil, segundo a plataforma internacional IQAir. Por volta das 8h40 deste sábado, a capital registrava 657 pontos no índice de qualidade do ar, classificado como "perigoso".
articles.summary: A fumaça em Manaus deixou a qualidade do ar em nível perigoso neste sábado, liderando o ranking de poluição no Brasil e gerando alertas severos de saúde.
articles.body:
Imagens feitas por drone mostram a fumaça das queimadas encobrindo a Avenida Max Teixeira, no bairro Cidade Nova, Zona Norte de Manaus , na manhã deste sábado (17). A fumaça reduziu a visibilidade na região e deixou o céu acinzentado .

O vídeo foi gravado por Alcides Neto durante um sobrevoo por volta das 6h20. As imagens também mostram uma camada espessa de fumaça em diferentes pontos próximos à avenida, inclusive em áreas residenciais .

Registro foi feito quando Manaus no topo do ranking de cidades com pior qualidade do ar do Brasil , segundo a plataforma internacional IQAir. O índice de qualidade do ar (AQI+) subiu de 441 pontos , às 6h, para 657 às 8h40, classificado como "perigoso" .

A concentração de partículas finas de poluição (PM2.5) era de 404,3 microgramas por metro cúbico (µg/m³) , o equivalente a 80,9 vezes a diretriz anual de concentração recomendada pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) .

Porto Velho (RO) aparecia em segundo lugar no ranking brasileiro, com 60 pontos no índice de qualidade do ar.

Órgãos emitem alertas e orientam população a se proteger da fumaça

Por volta das 8h13 deste sábado, a Defesa Civil do Estado emitiu um alerta de risco severo para a qualidade do ar . Diante da fumaça, o órgão recomendou o uso de máscara ao sair de casa e que os moradores evitem a exposição ao poluente .

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelo número 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193 .

A Prefeitura de Manaus também publicou orientações para reduzir a exposição à fumaça das queimadas. Entre as recomendações estão beber bastante água, manter portas e janelas fechadas e umidificar os ambientes .

O município orientou ainda o uso de máscara ao sair de casa e a evitar atividades físicas ao ar livre . A prefeitura também alertou que provocar queimadas é crime e pediu que os casos sejam denunciados pelo telefone 153 ou pelo site: slim.manaus.am.gov.br .

Moradores relatam fumaça intensa e dificuldade para respirar

Nas redes sociais, moradores de Manaus relataram cheiro forte de fumaça, ardência nos olhos e dificuldade para respirar neste sábado. Algumas publicações descreveram o episódio como o pior já vivido na capital.

"Mais um dia acordando com o fedor insuportável de fumaça. a qualidade do ar em manaus continua péssima e, mais uma vez, volto a dizer que sinto que estão tentando nos matar sufocados", escreveu um usuário na rede social X .

Outro morador relatou que a fumaça prejudicava a visibilidade: "Hoje de longe o pior dia pra se estar em Manaus, a fumaça é tão forte, fedorenta e densa que até a visibilidade tá afetada".

"O pior limiar de todos os episódios de fumaça na cidade", publicou outra pessoa.

Também houve relatos de ardência nos olhos mesmo dentro de casa e críticas à atuação das autoridades. "Arrisco dizer que hoje é o pior dia de Manaus no quesito poluição, os olhos ardem dentro de casa. E o pior: os governantes não estão levando o assunto tão a sério como deveria ser", escreveu um usuário.

Outras publicações apontaram a percepção de piora ao longo dos dias. "Parece que Manaus amanhece cada dia pior com essa fumaça", afirmou uma pessoa.

Em outra mensagem, um usuário descreveu a dificuldade para respirar na capital: "Manaus, 17 de outubro de 2026. tá dificílimo respirar, uma forte fumaça se espalhou por toda a cidade".

Fumaça cobre Manaus novamente neste sábado (17). — Foto: Alcides Neto

articles.title: Queimadas no Amazonas: fumaça impede voos de combate a incêndios | G1
articles.standfirst: Em nota, o Ibama explicou que as aeronaves precisam cumprir requisitos mínimos de visibilidade para voar com segurança. Quando a fumaça impede que esses limites sejam atingidos, as operações são suspensas.
articles.summary: Devido à baixa visibilidade, o Ibama suspendeu voos de combate às queimadas no Amazonas, enquanto Manaus registra índices de qualidade do ar perigosos.
articles.body:
A fumaça dos incêndios florestais no Amazonas reduziu a visibilidade e dificultou as operações aéreas de combate às chamas neste sábado (17), segundo o Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama). As condições impediram voos nos dois aeroportos utilizados pelas equipes em Manaus e a retomada depende da melhora da visibilidade .

A operação faz parte de uma força-tarefa do governo federal para combater os incêndios no estado , que também provocam a piora da qualidade do ar. Neste sábado, Manaus registrou novamente o pior índice de qualidade do ar entre as capitais brasileiras , segundo a plataforma internacional IQAir. O índice subiu de 441 pontos, às 6h, para 657 às 8h40, classificado como "perigoso" .

Em nota, o Ibama explicou que as aeronaves precisam cumprir requisitos mínimos de visibilidade para voar com segurança . Quando a fumaça impede que esses limites sejam atingidos, as operações são suspensas .

A expectativa do órgão é que as condições melhorem ao longo do dia, permitindo a retomada dos voos. O avião KC-390, da Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) , também v oltará a operar após a conclusão de serviços de manutenção .

Aeronaves são distribuídas entre Manaus e o interior

O Ibama informou que ajustou a distribuição das aeronaves usadas no combate aos incêndios, levando em conta as condições atmosféricas e o alcance dos equipamentos.

O planejamento prevê a seguinte estrutura:

Parintins : dois aviões Air Tractor, a partir de domingo (18);

Itacoatiara : dois aviões Air Tractor e uma aeronave da Defesa Civil estadual;

Manaus: dois aviões Air Tractor, um KC-390 e três helicópteros.

Os aviões Air Tractor são usados para lançar água sobre as áreas atingidas pelo fogo. O KC-390 pode despejar grandes volumes de água ou líquido retardante de chamas.

Já os helicópteros transportam brigadistas e equipamentos e dão apoio às equipes em solo.

Fumaça já havia prejudicado operações aéreas

Na segunda-feira (12), a fumaça também impediu parte das operações aéreas de combate aos incêndios no Amazonas . Naquele dia, segundo informações divulgadas pelo Ibama, apenas o KC-390 e três helicópteros conseguiram voar . Os helicópteros foram usados em missões de apoio logístico.

Ainda na segunda-feira, aeronaves do Ibama lançaram mais de 10 mil litros de água sobre focos de incêndio na Região Metropolitana de Manaus . Até aquela tarde, as equipes haviam acumulado 67,2 horas de voo.

Ao todo, o reforço federal anunciado para o estado inclui seis aviões Air Tractor, um KC-390, três helicópteros e um avião Caravan, usado em atividades de logística.

Órgãos emitem alertas e orientam população a se proteger da fumaça

Por volta das 8h13 deste sábado, a Defesa Civil do Estado emitiu um alerta de risco severo para a qualidade do ar . Diante da fumaça, o órgão recomendou o uso de máscara ao sair de casa e que os moradores evitem a exposição ao poluente .

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelo número 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193 .

A Prefeitura de Manaus também publicou orientações para reduzir a exposição à fumaça das queimadas. Entre as recomendações estão beber bastante água, manter portas e janelas fechadas e umidificar os ambientes .

O município orientou ainda o uso de máscara ao sair de casa e a evitar atividades físicas ao ar livre. A prefeitura também alertou que provocar queimadas é crime e pediu que os casos sejam denunciados pelo telefone 153 ou pelo site : slim.manaus.am.gov.br .

articles.title: Naufrágio no Rio Solimões em Tabatinga: 9 pessoas são resgatadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre os passageiros estavam indígenas da etnia Tikuna e cidadãos peruanos, incluindo duas crianças e duas mulheres. Após o resgate, o grupo foi levado para uma área de praia em trecho raso do rio.
articles.summary: Naufrágio no Rio Solimões em Tabatinga termina com resgate de nove pessoas, incluindo indígenas Tikuna e crianças que viajavam sem coletes salva-vidas.
articles.body:
Naufrágio em Tabatinga não deixou feridos, mas trouxe prejuízos. — Foto: Divulgação/Defesa Civil

Uma canoa do tipo "canoão" naufragou na tarde de sexta-feira (16) no Rio Solimões, em frente à aldeia Belém do Solimões, em Tabatinga, no interior do Amazonas. A embarcação transportava nove pessoas e uma carga de mercadorias. Todos os ocupantes foram resgatados sem ferimentos pela Defesa Civil do município.

Entre os passageiros estavam indígenas da etnia Tikuna e cidadãos peruanos, incluindo duas crianças e duas mulheres. Após o resgate, o grupo foi levado para uma área de praia em trecho raso do rio.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, a embarcação saiu de Tabatinga na manhã de sexta-feira com destino a São Paulo de Olivença. O naufrágio ocorreu quando o grupo se aproximava da aldeia Belém do Solimões e foi atingido por ventos fortes e banzeiros.

A canoa transportava alimentos, folhas de zinco, peças de ferro e combustível. De acordo com a Defesa Civil, nenhum dos passageiros usava colete salva-vidas.

A embarcação, o motor rabeta e parte da carga foram recuperados. Após o resgate, a equipe orientou os passageiros a passarem a noite na aldeia Belém do Solimões e retomarem a viagem apenas durante o dia.

Alimentos, folhas de zinco e outros insumos caíram no rio devido ao naufrágio. — Foto: Divulgação/Defesa Civil

Defesa Civil auxiliou também na recuperação dos insumos. — Foto: Divulgação/Defesa Civil

articles.title: Carros da prefeitura de Juazeiro do Norte são recuperados após furto | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois suspeitos foram identificados. Além dos dois veículos, uma moto com registro de roubo ou furto também foi recuperada na ação policial.
articles.summary: Dois suspeitos foram identificados. Além dos dois veículos, uma moto também foi recuperada. O caso ocorreu na última semana.
articles.body:
Dois carros da frota municipal da Prefeitura de Juazeiro do Norte , no Cariri cearense, foram recuperados após terem sido furtados do pátio de um centro administrativo da cidade. Uma motocicleta também foi recuperada durante a ação. Dois suspeitos foram presos na ação policial.

Conforme apuração da TV Verdes Mares, um dos veículos da prefeitura foi recuperado na última quinta-feira (15) por policiais em uma casa no Conjunto Padre Cícero, no Bairro Monsenhor Francisco Murilo de Sá Barreto. A partir disso, uma equipe do Grupamento Ambiental Metropolitano (GAM) de Juazeiro do Norte passou a monitorar o local.

Veículos da Prefeitura de Juazeiro do Norte são recuperados. — Foto: Reprodução

Durante o monitoramento, por volta das 3h desta sexta (16), os agentes flagraram a chegada de um jovem em um carro de cor branca com placa adulterada. Ao ser abordado, as equipes descobriram que a placa original do veículo pertence à frota da Secretaria de Educação de Juazeiro do Norte.

O suspeito, identificado como José Wellington Ferreira da Silva, de 23 anos, confessou ter sido chamado por outro homem para realizar os furtos no centro administrativo da prefeitura. O outro suspeito foi identificado como William Gomes Ribeiro, de 26 anos.

Na casa de William, os guardas municipais apreenderam uma motocicleta de cor azul que também apresentava registro de furto/roubo. O suspeito foi levado para a delegacia para prestar depoimento.

Suspeitos de furto foram identificados por guardas municipais. — Foto: Reprodução

Moto furtada também foi recuperada. O veículo não pertence à prefeitura. — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Golpe da moto em Alenquer: suspeito foge sem pagar hotel no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem recebeu R$ 2 mil de adiantamento por veículo e desapareceu durante a madrugada no oeste do Pará.
articles.summary: Golpe da moto em Alenquer deixa prejuízo de R$ 2 mil a morador e dívida em hotel após suspeito fugir durante a madrugada no oeste do Pará.
articles.body:
Moradores do município de Alenquer, no oeste do Pará, relatam ter sido vítimas de um esquema de estelionato envolvendo a falsa venda de motocicletas. Além de enganar compradores na região, o suspeito deixou um prejuízo financeiro em um hotel onde estava hospedado, fugindo do local de madrugada sem acertar as contas.

De acordo com o relato de um jovem que trabalhava em um bar na cidade, um cliente que frequentava o estabelecimento com assiduidade ofereceu a ele uma motocicleta pelo valor de R$ 6.500,00. Como não possuía o montante necessário para a aquisição, o funcionário repassou a proposta ao seu tio, que demonstrou interesse no negócio.

Suspeito fugiu pela madrugada de Alenquer — Foto: Câmeras de Segurança

Após acertar os detalhes, o vendedor exigiu o pagamento de uma entrada no valor de R$ 2.000,00. Após receber a quantia, o suspeito desapareceu sem entregar o veículo e sem dar qualquer tipo de justificativa sobre os valores ou o paradeiro da moto.

A fuga do suspeito ocorreu durante a madrugada. Ele estava hospedado em um hotel da cidade e deixou o estabelecimento sem pagar a conta, gerando um prejuízo de R$ 800,00 em diárias e serviços.

A proprietária do hotel contou que também foi alvo das investidas do suspeito. Segundo ela, o homem tentou aplicar o mesmo esquema e lhe fez uma proposta de venda de outra motocicleta, avaliada em R$ 4 mil, negócio que acabou não se concretizando.

Os casos foram expostos por moradores para alertar a comunidade sobre a atuação do suspeito na cidade. As autoridades policiais orientam que vítimas de estelionato registrem boletim de ocorrência na delegacia local para que os crimes sejam formalmente investigados.

articles.title: Algodão colorido verde: Paraíba tem produção pioneira no país | G1
articles.standfirst: Cultivo é feito por agricultores familiares no reassentamento Acauã e abastece empresa espanhola que fabrica roupas e tecidos orgânicos.
articles.summary: Cultivado por famílias em Itatuba, o algodão colorido verde é pioneiro no Brasil e abastece empresa espanhola de tecidos orgânicos sem uso de corantes.
articles.body:
Paraíba começa a produzir algodão colorido verde em Itatuba, no Agreste — Foto: Reprodução/Empaer

A Paraíba começou a colher algodão colorido verde no reassentamento Acauã, em Itatuba , no Agreste do estado. A produção é pioneira no país e faz parte do projeto Algodão Paraíba, iniciativa que incentiva o cultivo agroecológico por agricultores familiares e garante a comercialização da matéria-prima.

A produção é adquirida pela empresa espanhola Organic Cotton Colours (OCC), que fabrica roupas e tecidos com algodão orgânico. Por ter coloração natural, a fibra pode ser utilizada na indústria têxtil sem a necessidade de tingimento artificial, reduzindo o uso de produtos químicos nesse processo.

Segundo Paulo Emílio, gerente regional da Empresa Paraibana de Pesquisa, Extensão Rural e Regularização Fundiária (Empaer) em Itabaiana , o projeto beneficia mais de 70 famílias da agricultura familiar na região. A expectativa é produzir cerca de 30 toneladas de algodão colorido agroecológico nos cinco municípios atendidos pela iniciativa.

Algodão colorido gera renda e segurança alimentar

Algodão colorido gera renda e segurança alimentar — Foto: Reprodução/Empaer

Além de comercializar a fibra, os agricultores cultivam alimentos na mesma área, em um sistema conhecido como consórcio de culturas. Entre os produtos plantados estão milho, feijão, fava, gergelim, abóbora e amendoim.

A estratégia permite que as famílias obtenham renda com a venda do algodão e, ao mesmo tempo, garantam alimentos para o próprio consumo e para comercialização.

O trabalho também é organizado de forma coletiva, com grupos de agricultores que compartilham as atividades de preparo do solo, plantio e manejo das lavouras. Segundo o gerente regional, a colaboração ajuda a diminuir os custos de produção.

O projeto conta com assistência técnica e extensão rural da Empaer, que orienta os produtores durante o cultivo. Outro diferencial é a comercialização antecipada: as empresas compradoras estabelecem contratos com os agricultores antes do plantio, com definição de preço e quantidade.

“Então, o agricultor planta sabendo por quanto vai vender, esse preço não tem variação, porque assinou o contrato”, disse o gerente.

Cultivo agroecológico dispensa agrotóxicos

Coloração natural do algodão representa uma vantagem para a indústria têxtil, por dispensar o tingimento artificial da fibra — Foto: Reprodução/Empaer

As variedades de algodão colorido cultivadas na Paraíba foram desenvolvidas por meio de pesquisas da Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa Agropecuária (Embrapa), incluindo a unidade Embrapa Algodão, localizada no estado.

Entre elas estão a BRS Rubi, de fibra marrom, e a BRS Verde, que permite a produção de algodão com tonalidade verde. As variedades ampliam as possibilidades de comercialização da fibra para mercados interessados em matérias-primas produzidas com menor impacto ambiental.

De acordo com Paulo Emílio, o cultivo incentivado pelo projeto é realizado sem o uso de agrotóxicos e fertilizantes químicos.

“Esse algodão, além de ser colorido, ele é agroecológico e orgânico”, afirmou.

A coloração natural também representa uma vantagem para a indústria têxtil, porque dispensa o tingimento artificial da fibra. O processo convencional pode envolver o uso de substâncias químicas e gerar resíduos que afetam o meio ambiente.

Projeto é desenvolvido na região desde 2009

Projeto 'Algodão Paraíba' começou a ser desenvolvido na região de Itabaiana em 2009 — Foto: Reprodução/Empaer

O projeto Algodão Paraíba começou a ser desenvolvido na região de Itabaiana em 2009 e, posteriormente, foi ampliado para outros municípios do estado. A iniciativa reúne agricultores familiares, assistência técnica pública e empresas interessadas na compra da produção.

Segundo Paulo Emílio, o interesse pelo algodão colorido orgânico no mercado internacional, especialmente na Europa, representa uma oportunidade para ampliar o cultivo na Paraíba.

Com o início da colheita da variedade verde em Itatuba, a produção paraibana amplia as possibilidades de uso do algodão colorido e fortalece uma alternativa de geração de renda para a agricultura familiar, associando a comercialização da fibra ao cultivo de alimentos e a práticas agroecológicas.

articles.title: ICIA está entre as 100 melhores ONGs do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Entidade também foi apontada como a melhor de Pernambuco. O Prêmio Melhores ONGs reconhece organizações do terceiro setor que se destacam pela qualidade de sua atuação e por boas práticas de gestão.
articles.summary: Entidade também foi apontada como a melhor de Pernambuco. O Prêmio Melhores ONGs reconhece organizações do terceiro setor que se destacam pela qualidade de sua atuação e por boas p
articles.body:
Instituto do Câncer Infantil do Agreste — Foto: Assessoria/Divulgação

O Instituto do Câncer Infantil do Agreste (ICIA), com sede em Caruaru , está entre as 100 melhores Organizações Não Governamentais (ONGs) do Brasil e foi reconhecido como o melhor de Pernambuco.

Promovido nacionalmente, o Prêmio Melhores ONGs reconhece organizações do terceiro setor que se destacam pela qualidade de sua atuação e por boas práticas de gestão. O objetivo é valorizar instituições comprometidas com a transparência, a responsabilidade e a transformação social.

A avaliação considera cinco eixos principais: causa e estratégia de atuação; representação e responsabilidade; gestão e planejamento; estratégia de financiamento; e comunicação e prestação de contas.

“Receber esse reconhecimento entre as 100 Melhores ONGs do Brasil, pelo sexto ano consecutivo, e ser destacado como a melhor ONG de Pernambuco é motivo de muita alegria e, acima de tudo, de gratidão. Essa conquista pertence a cada profissional, voluntário, parceiro e doador que caminha conosco. Trabalhamos diariamente para acolher famílias, levar esperança e garantir que crianças e adolescentes tenham acesso a um cuidado digno, humanizado e de qualidade. Esse reconhecimento também aumenta nossa responsabilidade de continuar avançando e transformando vidas”, destaca o Dr. Luiz Henrique, diretor-geral do ICIA.

articles.body: Russian president’s Vladimir Putin investment envoy Kirill Dmitriev has described US president Donald Trump’s decision to waive a fresh package of sanctions and tariffs against Russia as a “truly historic moment”. The remarks came after Washington suspended key provisions of legislation aimed at tightening economic pressure on Moscow over its war in Ukraine."The suspension of some of the provisions of the Graham Act marks an important and truly historic moment," Dmitriev said in a post on X on Saturday.The remarks came a day after the White House released an executive order in which Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States. The measures had been due to take effect under the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which Trump signed in mid-September.In his post, Dmitriev argued that the legislation could have severely disrupted economic ties between the two countries."The legislation, which underwent fundamental and deeply negative changes following Senator Graham's death, could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the United States to a complete halt, inflicting serious damage primarily on the US economy and global markets," he wrote in a post on X.He added, "Economic cooperation between Russia and the United States serves the interests of both nations, contributes to global economic stability, and lays the foundation for building trust and achieving lasting peace."The legislation, backed by the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina and Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal, was designed to intensify pressure on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine in 2022."Instead of sanctions and confrontation, we need dialogue, mutually beneficial cooperation, and shared responsibility for global stability," Dmitriev wrote.The legislation sought to authorise sanctions against Russian officials and banks, as well as vessels linked to the country's shadow fleet of oil tankers. It also provided for tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from major importers of Russian oil and gas, including countries continuing to purchase Russian energy or helping Moscow evade sanctions.China and India, two of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, had raised concerns over the proposed measures. Beijing opposed what it described as "long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law", while New Delhi warned that additional tariffs could affect bilateral ties.Trump's waiver drew criticism from US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, who accused the president of conceding to Moscow."Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer said in a statement.Trump said in the executive order that he had submitted a certification to Congress confirming that the waiver was in the US national interest. articles.title: By 2020, an eastern Washington historian had spent more than 30 years building his own Monticello; the replica was about 90% complete and he was still working
articles.summary: Explore how historian Dan Sisson dedicated over 30 years to construct Monticello West in Washington using 22,186 salvaged bricks, inspired by Thomas Jefferson's Monticello.
articles.body: The house stands south of Ford, a small community in Stevens County, Washington, on land between state property and the Spokane Indian Reservation. Its brick walls and front elevation follow Thomas Jefferson’s Monticello in Virginia, though it was built with scavenged materials rather than a contractor’s budget. The builder is Dan Sisson, a historian, author, and longtime Eastern Washington University professor. He calls the house Monticello West. Though largely complete, the house remains a work in progress. The Spokesman-Review and the Los Angeles Times both covered Sisson’s project, and InsideHook later summarized the Times profile. Together, the reports describe a project that would normally take a construction crew, which Sisson took on with help from family, friends, and some hired workers, using mostly salvaged and secondhand materials.From Jefferson scholar to congressional candidate in 1976According to his biographical note, Sisson was born in Washington, D.C. He holds a master’s degree and a PhD. The note adds that he ran for Congress in 1976. A summary of that profile says he visited Monticello as a child with his father, who said that any building he made should resemble it.Digging the foundation at 61 and still working at 82A Los Angeles Times profile reports that Sisson dug the foundation with a shovel and pickaxe at 61 and was 82 when the profile was published. The profile also reports that he designed Monticello West in the mid-1980s, bought the land near Ford in 1998, and moved in during 2002.The Los Angeles Times article “How do you build a replica of Monticello? Brick by scavenged brick” reported that the replica, known as Monticello West, was about 90% complete by April 2020. Over two years, Sisson collected about 30,000 used bricks from a Spokane redevelopment zone, making roughly 120 trips in a pickup that could carry up to 250 bricks at a time. Stevens County withheld permission for the project until Sisson showed his plans to the planning director.Scavenged wood, flooring and marble, and thousands of straightened nailsMaterials were the project’s biggest challenge. Contemporary reports say he scavenged wood, flooring, and marble, much of it free or cheap, and straightened thousands of old nails for reuse. His wife and son helped, as did other people drawn to the idea of a Monticello northwest of Spokane.Jefferson’s plan in 1792 to reuse about 60,000 bricksReusing brick is not a new habit at Monticello. In a letter from Thomas Jefferson to Stephen Willis, 12 November 1792, Jefferson wrote that he expected the demolition of old walls and an antechamber to yield about 60,000 bricks. The Thomas Jefferson Foundation’s Monticello Encyclopedia records that Stephen Willis, a brick mason, arrived at Monticello around 1770 to help build the South Pavilion and continued working there through 1778. In effect, Jefferson reused materials from one project to build another, much as Sisson did with salvaged bricks.Jefferson’s 13 May 1822 brick estimate for six West Portico columnsJefferson also worked out his brick needs on paper. In Thomas Jefferson’s Notes on Bricks Needed for Monticello Columns and Cisterns, dated 13 May 1822, he tallied headers and stretchers course by course for six Doric column shafts. The editors identify those shafts as belonging to the West Portico. Monticello Magazine reports that the West Portico columns were restored in 2013 to their original look during Jefferson’s time by stripping away the layers of white paint and restoring the original render with period-appropriate materials. The restored columns are built of molded brick finished with a render, a cheaper approach than solid stone. Both builders, separated by two centuries, solved the column problem by choosing a cheaper material and shaping it to fit.Jefferson’s construction timeline and Sisson’s approach Sisson himself draws the comparison. Sisson himself draws the comparison, telling the Spokesman-Review that Jefferson spent 43 years building his house, a span he offers as a parallel to his own long schedule. The earlier-mentioned letter from 1792 indicates the pace at which Jefferson was proceeding. In 1792, Jefferson planned the next phase of construction at Monticello, including digging the cellars in early April.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US and Iran both claim control of Strait of Hormuz amid attacks on vessels
articles.summary: Two vessels have been struck with naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz this week.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Dozens of ships were attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz in October as Iran and the United States compete to assert their authority over the waterway.

At least 12 ships were attacked in the week ending on October 16, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported late Friday, with one important caveat.

“UKMTO is struggling to accurately report true number of attacks with majority of vessels attacked refusing to report to UKMTO,” the maritime security organisation stated. It said it was aware of more incidents in the waterway via other sources but could not verify them due to a lack of information.

The same pattern has been true for the first half of October. The month has seen the highest number of ship attacks since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran, which began on February 28.

Of the 12 vessels that were confirmed attacked, the organisation said half continued to their destination or reached port. One sank, two were disabled, and three were either damaged or had an unconfirmed outcome.

The UKMTO also reported a new type of attack on Saturday. The master of a tanker said their vessel was hit by a rocket-propelled grenade (RPG) fired from a small boat 78 nautical miles (equivalent to about 144km) northeast of Saudi Arabia’s city of Jubail, Eastern province, resulting in damage to the aft port quarter.

In recent months, the US has managed to increase energy transits through the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways through a shuttle system coordinated with Arab powers . But volumes have oscillated weekly due to rising Iranian attacks.

Oil flows through Hormuz were at 11.6 million barrels per day (bpd) over the seven days to October 13. This was about 68 percent of the 17.1 million bpd pre-war baseline, according to Kpler figures.

On Friday, Brent crude also touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May in light of ongoing attacks. The situation has been exacerbated by the Iran-aligned Houthis’ attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and their capture of the Bab al-Mandeb strait. Expectations that the conflict between the US and Iran was escalating have also impacted prices.

The US military has provided a starkly different outlook on the situation in and around the Strait of Hormuz, which accounted for roughly a fifth of global oil and natural gas flows before the war began.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) chief Brad Cooper claimed in a video message late Friday that despite the Iranian attacks, 400 ships and 100 million barrels of oil moved through the Strait of Hormuz over the past week.

“Let me be clear: The Strait of Hormuz is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran,” he said, attributing the greatly increased ship attacks to “desperation” by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

The US military also claimed that it continues to prevent Iranian exports and imports via its southern ports through an “ironclad” naval blockade . It claims the blockade has cost Iran $25bn in oil export income, and that the US has recently seized $350m in Iranian cryptocurrency financing.

The UKMTO report said total outbound transit over the last seven days was 125 ships, with total inbound transits standing at 129. Over the week, most transits by the Western security agency were for dry bulk cargo, followed by tanker products and general cargo.

Tehran has not provided exact figures on how many vessels have been attacked, or how many are passing through the Hormuz, although it has said Washington is exaggerating numbers to project success of its naval campaign.

It comes as two vessels were reportedly hit by naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz this week, with the US and Iran offering contradictory claims about the situation.

The IRGC has increasingly reported that vessels are hitting mines across the strategic waterway, which it says remains unsafe for vessels which do not coordinate with Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority, an entity set up during the war to manage passage through the Hormuz.

The latest claim came on Saturday, when the IRGC said a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil caught fire after striking a mine while moving through an “unauthorised” route.

Iran’s state-run Press TV shared footage it says showed the tanker on fire. But CENTCOM said it had cleared the strait of naval mines, and that vessels are being struck by projectiles.

The latest incident “fact-checked” by the US military was on Thursday, when it said a civilian container ship, the M/V GFS Pride, was hit by an IRGC projectile, not by a mine as the Iranians had claimed. The vessel sank as it was being towed to shore.

The US has refrained from responding to any of the recent vessel attacks, but there are concerns that Washington could escalate the war after the November 3 midterm elections.

Diplomacy has not fully halted, with messages continuing to be relayed between the two parties by regional mediators like Pakistan, Qatar and others. But no breakthrough in talks is expected any time soon.

President Donald Trump has reportedly ordered the US military to remain prepared for launching bigger attacks after the elections. Those attacks could potentially include using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, nicknamed the “mother of all bombs” , according to US media.

But Tehran has signalled that it intends to continue the attacks, with acting Defence Minister Majid Ibn Reza saying on Saturday that it will be Iranian missiles, not US bombs, that determine the future of the war.

“Your bombs will explode elsewhere; in your global reputation, the US economy, and even your electoral calculations,” he was quoted as saying by state media.

articles.title: Changes made to plans for solar farm near Selby after opposition
articles.summary: The proposed scheme, near Selby, is facing a number of objections from residents and councillors.
articles.body:
Plans to build a battery energy storage system and 500MW solar farm across swathes of land near Selby could be changed following objections from people living nearby.

Light Valley Solar Limited wants to build on 2,520 acres (1,020 hectares) of land between the villages of Escrick, Monk Fryston, Hambleton, Chapel Haddlesey and South Milford.

The development has faced opposition, with conerns raised about the loss of agricultural land, the impact on the rural landscape and the potential harm to wildlife.

In response the firm has outlined nine proposed amendments, including removing solar panels from an area near homes, creating new wildlife habitats and altering construction access routes.

Opponents have also questioned the scale and location of the scheme, arguing that it would industrialise large areas of countryside and affect the character of nearby villages.

Among the changes to the scheme that have been proposed is the removal of solar panels from land south of Milford Lodge and Milford Lodge Cottage.

The land would instead become an area of grassland managed to provide habitat for ground-nesting birds.

The developer said the change followed discussions with North Yorkshire Council about bird habitat provision, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

In addition, the removal of panels would increase the distance between the development and Milford Lodge Cottage, following representations from residents.

The developer has also been in discussions with Sherburn Aero Club and says removing panels near a proposed emergency landing strip would improve safety for aircraft making emergency landings.

articles.title: The woman who remembers everything: What it’s like to live with memories of your best days — and worst nightmares
articles.summary: FIRST PERSON: Rebecca Sharrock tells Rachel Dobkin what it’s like living with Highly Superior Autobiographical Memory and how she deals with disturbing flash...
articles.body:
Rebecca Sharrock remembers almost every day of her life.

The 36-year-old has a rare condition called Highly Superior Autobiographical Memory, or HSAM, which means she can remember vivid details from her past — even back to when she was a young child.

"I live with constant random flashbacks of a clutter of experiences — negative, positive, mundane — and they just flash through my head all the time from random ages, such as they can jump from three years old to 20 years old to seven years old to 16 years old, and it's very difficult for me to get to sleep at night," Rebecca told The Independent from her home in Brisbane, Australia .

For Rebecca, who also has autism, anxiety and obsessive-compulsive disorder , it can be hard to let go of disturbing memories. She said HSAM and OCD "get along like a house on fire" and that the two conditions feed off each other.

"I find it hard to just let go of emotions, let go of thoughts, and with HSAM, it then extends to more and more memories that I can't let go of," Rebecca said.

While many people might retain a hazy memory of a day when a global event occurred, Rebecca can recount it with extraordinary precision.

When asked about August 31, 1997, the day when Princess Diana died, Rebecca remembered in detail how her family reacted to the tragic news.

"I was seven. I wasn't allowed to watch the news until I was 11 because mum said that it may be a bit scary for me, but I did catch a news story because my mum and my auntie were over, and me and my sister were having a bath, and mum was washing our hair, and then my auntie just called out, and she said, 'Oh, the Princess of Wales has died,'" Rebecca said.

Dr. Craig Stark is professor of neurobiology and behavior and principal investigator of Stark Lab at the University of California , Irvine. His team study HSAM and diagnosed Rebecca with the condition in 2013 when she was 23, after two years of testing.

Stark says that he and his team have validated memories of people with HSAM by asking about both public and private events.

"For a number of these folks...we can verify against actual public kinds of things," he told The Independent . "Some of them have had diaries, and it's like, 'Oh yeah, they could go back and study their diary.' Yep, they could, and then they show up with multiple boxes of diaries, and you're like, 'Oh.'"

HSAM is a rare condition where people have an exceptional ability to remember autobiographical memories. While Stark says that it's impossible to truly answer how many people have HSAM, researchers have identified about 100 people worldwide with the condition.

One famous example is the actress Marilu Henner, best known for the sitcom Taxi that ran from 1978 to 1983.

Henner offered a positive outlook on HSAM for students at the University of California, Davis, during a visit to one of psychology professor Charan Ranganath's classes last February.

"Developing a better autobiographical memory is the strongest defense against meaninglessness that we have. Because then our lives count for something," she said, according to the college's magazine .

Stark said that he and his team found that people with HSAM score high on obsessive-compulsive tendencies. The professor explained the process that people he's studied with HSAM go through to remember the days of their lives.

"They turn the day into basically the diary or the social media post version of the day," Stark said. "And that's what they remember very, very well. They think about it multiple times — repetition over time, repeated practice. They have a structure and everything to it. They link it to other events."

"We've known for thousands of years that these things improve your memory. And Marilu Henner is kind of right that the rest of us just don't do this. [People with HSAM] do, which then makes their memory for autobiographical events better," Stark explained.

Rebecca said that she loves to organize her memories, which she attributes to her OCD.

"It's as if in my head, hypothetically, I've got a filing cabinet, and I like to organize them into months, years and days," she said. "I had a fear as a child with my obsessive-compulsive disorder about forgetting things. So, when mum would say, 'You need to just put your memories into a box,' I'd say, 'But I'm scared that I'll forget them, and then a part of my life will be missing.'"

Rebecca is a lover of classical music and foreign languages, using her passions as a distraction from unwanted memories that constantly pop into her head.

She said that when she struggles to go to sleep at night, she listens to classical music. "I anchor my mind into relaxation by just imagining that my thoughts and feelings are the notes of the music, and that helps me a lot," she said.

Rebecca has taken medication to manage her OCD since she was 16 but stress can make some days harder than others.

Rebecca can't drive or have a traditional career because of her conditions.

"If I was to just have to be in one place all day and do what I have to do, I'm constantly having to ground my mind due to flashbacks," Rebecca said. "I've had to pick a job which is writing and doing creative work that relaxes my mind. So it still occupies me, but relaxes me. And learning languages distracts my mind from flashbacks because I have to focus on either learning the instrument or learning the language."

She has been taking classical guitar lessons for three years and will start violin lessons next year. She's also learned how to speak Spanish and French and is almost finished with her courses in Italian.

Rebecca released her first book, My Life is a Puzzle , in 2024, which gives a chronological account of her experiences from birth to age 30. She is working on her next book titled My Life in Sketches .

"For many years, I did wish that I was like most other people. I did wish that I didn't have OCD, didn't have these experiences of HSAM, didn't have my issues with autism, and that causes my anxiety primarily," Rebecca said. "I have thought over the past five years that because I've never known life to be any different…it would be unsettling to just have to suddenly adapt to a different life."

Rebecca hopes more research into HSAM can help better understand the brain. "We need to learn a lot more about what's in our world rather than what's outside of our world," she said.

articles.body: College football brings us a full slate of action this week. There are plenty of Top-25 teams taking the field, and multiple are even facing each other. This is one of the best schedules that I’ve seen in the past couple of years. However, I have one game that I’m focused on more than any other, as we have Florida going into Texas to take on the Longhorns. The Florida Gators are 4-2 for the season, and 2-2 in SEC play. If you watched them a few weeks ago, you would’ve thought they were the best team in the country. They absolutely destroyed Ole Miss, dropping them 52-28. However, their big win may have set them up for a letdown. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE They headed to Missouri the next week, and they got killed, losing 45-17. Florida gave up six unanswered scores. They had one touchdown in the last few seconds of the game, but clearly it was meaningless. You might’ve been able to say that the Gators were in a letdown spot after Ole Miss. However, that doesn’t explain how they were manhandled by the Gamecocks last week. South Carolina went into the swamp and beat the Gators 38-19. LaNorris Sellers, the quarterback from South Carolina, threw for four touchdowns and ran for another score. The Gators threw two interceptions and lost another ball via fumble. Florida just seems to have their offense stall out. They allowed the Gamecocks to score three straight touchdowns in the second half. FLORIDA DROPS IMPRESSIVE OFFENSIVE PERFORMANCE TO PULL OFF MASSIVE WIN OVER NO. 4 OLE MISS Texas was ranked #1 last week, and this week… not so much. They’ve fallen to #7 in the nation after losing last week to a vastly inferior Oklahoma team. Perhaps we all should’ve recognized this coming. The team faced Ohio State in Week 3, and they were getting crushed before some poor Buckeye play, and a good second half from the Longhorns gave them a one-point win. They dismissed UTSA fairly easily in Week 4. Coming off of a bye week, the Longhorns were able to narrowly escape Tennessee on the road. They won 20-17, but I could still give them credit for beating a ranked opponent on the road. Last week, though, was inexcusable. They lost 27-24 to an unranked Oklahoma team. Most of the damage came in the third quarter as the Sooner scored 17 unanswered points. Texas tied it up in the fourth quarter, but the defense allowed the team to get into field goal range, and the Sooners won. This game was technically a home game for Oklahoma, but it was played in Texas. At this point, you genuinely have to be concerned about something with Texas. Is Arch Manning really a great quarterback? Does the Texas defense have what they need, or is their head coach the main issue? I personally think the problem is their head coach. Manning needs to protect the ball better, and he had two interceptions against Oklahoma. articles.title: Hardline Israeli rabbi ruling on stolen Palestinian olives prompts uproar
articles.summary: A controversial ruling by a hardline Israeli rabbi has been condemned by Palestinians.
articles.body:
Prominent Israeli Rabbi Dov Lior issued a Jewish religious ruling on Friday permitting settlers to steal olives from Palestinian orchards in the occupied West Bank.

Lior’s ruling claims that Palestinian landowners who could not access their olives during the harvest season due to Israeli restrictions have been sufficiently compensated in the years they had access to the fruit. According to the ruling, Jews are permitted to pick these olives to claim ownership of the Palestinian land.

Lior, born in Poland in 1933, went as far as classifying the theft of olives from Palestinian farms as an “additional virtue”, as settler pogroms and Israeli occupation continue in the West Bank.

He added that settlers should “conquer the land” far from Jewish communities in order to publicly “demonstrate our ownership” and follow biblical commandment.

“The Jewish people have never given up on the Land of Israel, as we express in our prayers every single day,” the ruling continues. “The Arabs never purchased the land from the Jewish people or from any individual Jew, and therefore it is stolen land in their hands… They never bought it in any way and it remained under the ownership of the Jewish people.”

The ruling coincides with another wave of settler pogroms against Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest season. On Friday. at least 19 people were injured in 34 attacks by the Israeli military and settlers on Palestinians harvesting their crops across the West Bank.

An American photojournalist working for The Washington Post was assaulted by settlers while covering the daily violence, and five vehicles were torched.

Many Palestinian farmers have been unable to access their crops due to Israeli restrictions and the dangers from the settlers.

While settler pogroms are not exceptional, they come weeks before Israeli elections, with a push by far-right parties to gain the support of settlers and their supporters. But not all Jewish religious leaders backed the call to steal Palestinian olives.

Rabbis from the religious council of the Gush Etzion settlements published a letter calling the illegal harvesting of Palestinian crops theft, blasphemy, and a moral defect.

Tzohar, an organisation of 800 orthodox rabbis, said in a statement that only the state has the authority to confiscate property. As long as the state recognises Arab ownership of the olives, they belong to them, it added.

Mamoun Abu Amer, an analyst on Israeli politics, told Al Jazeera that there could be political reasons behind the religious groups’ rejection of Rabbi Dov Lior’s comments.

“The position of the other rabbis who rejected this call might be a move driven by political motive and pressure from entities within the government to give the impression that these are anomalous voices that do not represent the general opinion of the settlers.

“The Israeli government is trying to portray that those who carry out these riots are a limited-number group that does not represent public opinion in the settlements, and that the settlers are peaceful, good, and law-abiding, and that the issue is confined to the ‘ Hilltop Youth ‘ boys who commit these crimes,” he explained.

Rabbi Dov Lior holds immense influence among hardline settler groups, such as the Hilltop Youth, who fiercely back his hardline religious decrees that oppose any territorial compromise with Palestinians.

He is also a prominent figure within Israel’s Religious Zionist movement and serves as the spiritual guide for the far-right Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power) party, led by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.

“Ben-Gvir relies on the religious rulings of Rabbi Dov Lior, which rely on biblical texts and the Book of Deuteronomy,” Abu Amer noted. He claimed that Rabbi Lior adopts the most extreme interpretations in the Jewish religion.

“There is an important matter, which is that Ben-Gvir competes via the TikTok platform, propaganda, and populist rhetoric, and this is a rhetoric that serves him and brings him votes, given the environment and general atmosphere in Israel after the events of October 7, as there is a ‘market for extremism’ in the Israeli society,” Abu Amer added.

Knesset member Gilad Kariv of the left-wing Democrats Party criticised Lior, accusing him and his followers of dragging Israel into a flood of moral vice.

“Whoever stands on the sidelines in this issue joins the camp of Rabbi Dov Lior and his criminals,” Kariv said.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia’s Prince Sultan became the first Arab in space in 1985, observed Ramadan aboard Nasa’s Discovery and returned to a ticker-tape parade
articles.summary: In June 1985, Saudi Arabia’s Prince Sultan bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud travelled into space aboard the American Space Shuttle Discovery, becoming the
articles.body: In June 1985, Saudi Arabia’s Prince Sultan bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud travelled into space aboard the American Space Shuttle Discovery, becoming the first Arab in space. According to Astronautics and Aeronautics, 1985: A Chronology, his journey brought together two parts of his life that rarely shared the same setting: the responsibilities of a member of the Saudi royal family and the experience of seeing Earth from orbit. The mission also coincided with Ramadan, adding a personal and religious dimension to his time away from home. When he returned, the prince found himself at the centre of an unusually public reception in Saudi Arabia, where his achievement had attracted attention far beyond the world of space exploration.Prince Sultan’s historic journey aboard Space Shuttle DiscoveryPrince Sultan’s flight took place during the June 1985 mission of the Space Shuttle Discovery. His participation marked a first for the Arab world, while his position as a member of Saudi Arabia’s royal family gave the journey a particular significance at home. He travelled as a payload specialist, taking part in a Nasa mission rather than serving as a career astronaut.The flight offered Saudi Arabia a direct connection to the American space programme at a time when human spaceflight remained a relatively rare undertaking. For the prince, it was also an opportunity to experience a view of the planet that few people had seen for themselves.How Prince Sultan observed Ramadan while travelling in spaceThe timing of the mission presented Prince Sultan with a practical and personal challenge. His journey took place during Ramadan, the holiest month in Islam, when Muslims traditionally fast from dawn until sunset and observe daily prayers. Being aboard a spacecraft meant that some familiar religious practices had to be reconsidered.The prince sought guidance from Muslim scholars about how to observe his faith while in orbit. According to The Saudi Gazette report, he continued to pray five times a day and fasted for part of the flight. The normal reference points for prayer were complicated by the spacecraft’s movement around Earth, where the cycle of sunrise and sunset was far shorter than it was on the ground.With the spacecraft circling Earth, daylight and darkness alternated rapidly. The experience gave his religious observance an unfamiliar setting, combining a routine rooted in faith with the unusual conditions of space travel.Prince Sultan’s view of Earth from space changed how he saw the worldPrince Sultan’s descriptions of the view from orbit moved beyond individual countries and borders. He recalled how his perspective shifted over the course of the mission, from recognising particular places to taking in larger geographical features. Eventually, he said, the planet appeared as a single blue sphere moving against the darkness of space.Astronautics and Aeronautics, 1985: A Chronology, he said, "I had a small experience after I came back from space. ! I always jogged over the same area in Houston, sometimes 15 miles a day, but when I came back and jogged over the same course, I noticed at least 50 percent more things in nature."His observation was personal rather than a scientific conclusion about how spaceflight affects perception. Still, it offered a glimpse of how an extraordinary journey had influenced his everyday life. The streets and natural features were familiar, but his attention to them had changed.A public welcome awaited him back in Saudi ArabiaThe prince’s return home brought a reception that he described as unusual for the country. Saudi Arabia welcomed him with a ticker-tape parade, with crowds gathering to see him and helicopters dropping paper over the celebrations. He recalled people of different ages reaching out to greet him, describing a level of public emotion that surprised him.The response extended beyond the parade itself. According to the September 1985 report, his face appeared on thousands of T-shirts and letters arrived in large numbers, reportedly hundreds each day. His flight had become a widely recognised event in Saudi Arabia, turning a technical achievement in space exploration into a public occasion.Prince Sultan met President Reagan after his historic space missionDuring his visit to Washington after the mission, Prince Sultan gave interviews, attended receptions and met government officials, including President Ronald Reagan, as part of a goodwill tour, as reported by Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute. His appearances gave American audiences an opportunity to hear directly from the Saudi royal who had taken part in the shuttle flight.In the newspaper interview, he also spoke about his life outside official engagements. He described himself as a bachelor who did not drink or smoke, adding that these habits did not make him a dull person. The remark offered a lighter glimpse of his personality amid discussions of religion, international relations and the experience of travelling into space.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2022, California launched a floating salmon-collection experiment in Shasta Reservoir; redesigns reduced predator encounters and increased the number of endangered fish collected
articles.summary: California's innovative floating salmon-collection system at Shasta Reservoir has shown promising results in enhancing the collection of endangered winter-run Chinook salmon and reducing predator encounters, paving the way for fish recovery efforts.
articles.body: In 2022, California launched a trial floating system in Shasta Reservoir to help restore endangered winter-run Chinook salmon to their habitat in the McCloud River. The California Department of Water Resources led the four-year pilot project. It tested whether young salmon migrating downstream could be collected before dispersing into the reservoir and transported around Shasta Dam. The construction of Shasta and Keswick dams in the 1940s blocked access to high-elevation, cold-water rivers where Chinook salmon spawned. In an update in January 2026, DWR reported that redesigning and relocating the collection system lessened predator presence around it and increased the number of fish collected. These improvements represent progress in testing a fish-passage strategy, though they do not yet demonstrate that the fish population has recovered.Why California developed a floating salmon-collection systemWinter-run Chinook salmon reportedly used the upper Sacramento River watershed, which included the McCloud River for spawning and early development. The fish population was left dependent on areas downstream of the dams after the construction of Shasta and Keswick dams, as they blocked their access to these upstream habitats. These lower-elevation waters can be challenging to manage during droughts and periods of high temperatures. According to DWR, climate change and drought place additional pressure on the species because warmer water can threaten the survival of eggs and young fish. Therefore, restoring access to colder historical habitat is a part of a broader effort to improve the population’s resilience to changing environmental conditions.The central challenge faced by the project is getting juvenile salmon out of the McCloud River before they enter the much larger Shasta Reservoir. The Juvenile Salmonid Collection System (JSCS) uses a floating structure, guidance nets, a temperature curtain, a debris boom and a fish trap to direct migrating fish towards a collection point. Once captured, the young fish can be placed in transport containers and moved downstream around the dams, thus allowing them to continue their journey towards the Pacific Ocean.From initial testing to redesigningThe project received $1.5 million in funding in February 2022. Following this, DWR began testing the first version of the collection system in September. During the initial phase, engineers and biologists evaluated the system’s hydraulic performance and temperature conditions. In 2022, no salmon were collected, as the priority was to test how the structure operated and determine how its position and layout could be improved.In 2023, the project expanded to include juvenile salmon collection. DWR also conducted “efficiency releases,” in which hatchery-raised, tagged juvenile salmon were released upstream of the system so researchers could measure how many were captured later on. To evaluate the performance of the physical structure, the engineering team conducted efficiency releases by tracking hatchery-raised juvenile salmon introduced upstream of the JSCS and measuring the exact number successfully gathered in the trap.According to the state agency’s January 2026 data, information gathered during the pilot project informed an improved second version of the system in late 2025. Additionally, the department moved the collector from its earlier position where the McCloud River meets the reservoir into the river environment itself. The changes reportedly reduced predator presence near the system and increased collection numbers.What the results mean for salmon recoveryThe larger reintroduction program seeks to repopulate winter-run Chinook salmon in their native range above Shasta Dam, while enabling their offspring to migrate downstream to the ocean. According to the 2026 report, at least two pairs of adult winter-run Chinook salmon have migrated from the lake back into the McCloud River to breed. While the migration of these adult fish is promising for the reintroduction project, it does not provide evidence that the collection system alone led to their migration.The project has involved DWR, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, NOAA Fisheries, the Winnemem Wintu Tribe, the US Fish and Wildlife Service and other partners. This partnership brings together engineering, fisheries science, and Indigenous knowledge to tackle the problems created by the dams.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Albania sees fresh clashes as student-led movement targets PM Rama
articles.summary: Thousands of young people gathered outside Albania’s Education Ministry in central Tirana on Saturday, marking the fifth consecutive day of a growing
articles.body: Thousands of young people gathered outside Albania’s Education Ministry in central Tirana on Saturday, marking the fifth consecutive day of a growing student-led movement calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.The demonstration turned violent when a group of masked youths threw rocks at riot police. Officers responded by firing stun grenades and tear gas and deploying a water cannon.Protests over alleged corruption and a shortage of jobs have begun spreading across Albania. In Tirana, demonstrators smashed windows, set government buildings on fire and clashed with security personnel during the week, according to the Reuters.According to police figures, around 500 protesters had been detained so far, of whom 330 were subsequently released. Authorities recorded injuries to approximately 120 police officers and 45 demonstrators, although the actual number of injured protesters could be higher because some cases may have gone unreported.The unrest represents the most significant challenge to Rama since he took office in 2013. His Socialist Party secured a fourth consecutive term in last year’s elections.Luxury resort controversy preceded student protestsThe current unrest follows months of largely peaceful demonstrations triggered by plans to construct a luxury resort along Albania’s unspoilt southern coastline. The project has received backing from investors, including Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.Villagers told Reuters in July that their land had been wrongfully sold for the proposed development. A subsequent Reuters report found that the individual who sold the land was wanted by prosecutors on suspicion of drug trafficking, allegations denied by his lawyer.Reuters found no evidence of wrongdoing by Kushner, who is not directly involved in the villagers’ dispute.Rama’s government has faced repeated corruption scandals. Analysts have also described Albania as a centre for criminal groups seeking to launder proceeds from drug and weapons trafficking, issues that have complicated the country’s efforts to join the European Union.Rama vows to protect right to protestRama, who denies wrongdoing and told Reuters earlier this week that he would not resign, said on Saturday that his government respected the students and would safeguard their right to demonstrate.“My responsibility is even clearer during these difficult times ... to protect our citizens, guarantee justice, and move Albania forward — together with this governing majority, which holds a very clear mandate: to see Albania in the European Union by 2030,” he wrote on Facebook.Albania, alongside Montenegro, is among the leading candidates in the EU accession process in the Western Balkans.Protests spread across EuropeThe unrest in Albania comes amid growing demonstrations in other European countries over public services, living costs and housing.In France, high-school students have been protesting for weeks to demand more teachers and improved school facilities. The movement appears to be attracting support from other sections of society.Spain has also witnessed widespread demonstrations this month over soaring rents and a shortage of affordable housing, prompting the government to call a snap election.You use AI every day. articles.title: Child, four women among Palestinians injured in West Bank pogroms
articles.summary: Attacks follow a religious edict by a prominent far-right rabbi permitting the seizure of Palestinian olives.
articles.body:
Several Palestinians have been injured by Israeli settlers, and farmers have been arrested by Israeli forces during Israeli pogroms across the occupied West Bank.

Four women and a child were among six people injured on Saturday when Israeli settlers attacked residents in Ma’in village in the Masafer Yatta area, south of Hebron, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS).

In the town of Deir Ammar, west of Ramallah, Israeli forces opened fire on farmers picking olives, forcing them to leave their land, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa.

In the same area, Israeli settlers shot and injured two Palestinians. In the village of Tuqu, southeast of Bethlehem, Israeli forces fired on a Palestinian civilian vehicle.

In the village of Kafr Malek, northeast of Ramallah, settlers raided a farm at dawn and killed about 20 sheep, Mayor Najeh Rustum told Al Jazeera.

He added that Israeli forces had raided the village the previous night as well, firing tear gas canisters that ignited a fire in a house and caused material damage.

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah, said settlers destroyed olive trees across the Beit Furik plain, east of Nablus, in the northern West Bank while Israeli forces arrested landowners and olive pickers.

In the village of Deir Jarir, east of Ramallah, she said, settlers under army protection fired live ammunition at farmers in the al-Hariq area to prevent them from completing the harvest and forced them off their land. Settlers also smashed the vehicle of international activist Jonathan Budlak in the village and threw stones at a farmer’s vehicle.

In the village of Burqa near Ramallah, Israeli forces and settlers prevented farmers from picking olives, Odeh said, adding that settlers attacked farmers in the Wadi al-Sha’er area, southeast of Salfit.

“What we see, whether it’s in Beit Furik, Kafr Malek, Deir Jarir or elsewhere in the occupied West Bank, is part of a campaign,” Odeh said.

She said settlers have become increasingly emboldened, publicly advertising attack campaigns on social media platforms.

“There have been 300 documented attacks since the beginning of October, and that has had a devastating impact on a very important season for Palestinian farmers,” she said, adding that danger comes from soldiers and settlers alike as military forces routinely intervene to protect settlers and attack Palestinians defending their land.

The attacks follow a religious edict issued by Rabbi Dov Lior, a prominent rabbi for National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power party and a leading authority among the Hilltop Youth , which is a religious Zionist group devoted to seizing Palestinian land in the West Bank.

In the edict, Lior stated that harvesting olives in the Holy Land is entirely permitted and carries an added virtue, given security dangers.

He wrote that Jews are permitted to harvest olives even in areas far from Jewish communities to publicly display ownership of the land and fulfil God’s commandment of conquering it. He claimed the land belongs to the Jewish people and Palestinians did not buy or rent it.

Odeh said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu downplays pogroms and no concrete action is taken to stop them.

“It is a matter of debate among politicians, but no one is stopping these settlers, whose names, locations and homes are known,” she said, adding that politicians permit the violence to continue because “it is politically expedient” and secures votes before elections on October 27.

articles.title: 'An evening in Paris': Opposition questions 'nature' of Punjab CM Mann's France visit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's visit to Paris has drawn sharp criticism from opposition leaders, with the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's visit to Paris has drawn sharp criticism from opposition leaders, with the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal questioning the purpose of his trip while raising concerns over drug abuse and law and order in Punjab. The backlash comes as the state government faces scrutiny over recent killings linked to the state's drug menace, with the Union home ministry seeking reports on the cases.BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh alleged that Mann's foreign trip, which he said coincided with the chief minister's birthday, was inappropriate at a time when Punjab was facing multiple crises.BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh alleged that Mann's foreign trip, which he said coincided with the chief minister's birthday, was inappropriate at a time when Punjab was facing multiple crises.""Punjab is burning in the fire of drug addiction; law and order have completely collapsed... 23 police stations have been targeted in grenade attacks, and even police personnel feel unsafe while in uniform. At a time when all of Punjab is engulfed in a raging crisis, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has chosen to travel to France with his wife to celebrate his birthday. This is a deeply distressing situation," Chugh said on Saturday.Questioning the nature of the visit, the BJP leader alleged, "If this is an official state visit, how is his wife accompanying him? In reality, a birthday party is being hosted in France under the guise of an official state visit."Chugh also targeted the AAP government over the drug menace and security concerns, claiming that people opposing drug abuse were being killed and citing grenade attacks on police stations. "Punjab is burning in the fire of drug addiction; law and order have completely collapsed," he said, alleging that even police personnel felt unsafe.The chief minister also faced criticism from Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia, who alleged that Mann had attended a police meeting in Phillaur on October 16 while under the influence of alcohol. The allegation has not been independently verified.Referring to Mann's birthday and his trip to Paris, Majithia said, "Today is his birthday. I even tweeted today about 'An Evening in Paris', which is a famous Hindi song, 'Rang-rangiliyan manane gaye hain'."Majithia questioned the chief minister's handling of the drug issue, alleging that Mann had attended a meeting on the menace while intoxicated."Holding a meeting against drugs while being drunk as the Chief Minister, what on earth is happening?" he said.Separately, Congress leader Sachin Pilot criticised the Punjab government's handling of law and order, alleging that killings, extortion, ransom demands and encounters had become common in the state.Speaking during a visit to Moga district on Saturday, Pilot called for accountability and faster legal action in murder cases. He also referred to a family that, he alleged, had been waiting for justice and assistance three years after the death of a young man's father.The opposition attacks come amid continuing criticism of the AAP government over drug abuse, gang violence and security in Punjab. The allegations against Mann and his government form part of the opposition's broader challenge to the state's handling of law and order.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: UK must protect against Russian 'hybrid attacks', ex-national security adviser says
articles.summary: Lord Ricketts says more should be spent on improving the resilience of energy, transport, air traffic control and defence sites.
articles.body:
The government must do more to protect key infrastructure against "hybrid attacks" from Russia, a former national security adviser has told the BBC.

Lord Ricketts said more money should be spent on the defence budget, as well as improving the resilience of energy, transport and air traffic control.

He warned hybrid attacks were becoming "more reckless, more dangerous" and that people could end up being killed.

It comes after MI5 chief Sir Kevin McCallum said in his annual speech earlier this week that threats from foreign states, including Russia and Iran, had quadrupled in the last decade .

Lord Ricketts told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that ministers had to warn British people about what might be coming.

"Not only is [Russian President Vladimir] Putin trying to break morale in Ukraine, he's also trying to undermine morale in European countries," he said.

He said there had been a stark warning from the head of MI5 that there could be worse to come in terms of hybrid attacks in the UK or on other Nato territory.

Responding to a question about the impact of disruption by Russia, Lord Ricketts said: "I'm not saying there's going to be industrial war with tanks rolling across the north German plain.

"But yes these hybrid attacks are getting more reckless, more dangerous...people are going to end up getting killed somewhere."

Hybrid attacks tend to use non-military methods, such as hacking, in an attempt to destabilise a country.

Moscow is suspected to be behind many such attacks in Europe since the start of the war in Ukraine, but it has always denied involvement.

As well as cyber-attacks, hybrid attacks can include attempts at sabotage and efforts to spread misinformation.

Lord Ricketts's warning comes after US President Donald Trump blocked sanctions on Russia . Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said the decision "only encourages him [Putin] to keep attacking" Ukraine.

The former national security adviser, who also previously ran the Foreign Office, said the UK's focus should be on putting more effort into the coalition of the willing, rather than attempting to act as a bridge between Zelensky and Trump.

"I don't think in Trump's current mood there is any influence Britain can have in the short term," he said.

A growing number of European leaders have warned that Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine.

Last month, Germany said Russia was responsible for a drone attack on an airport in Leipzig , in which an explosive failed to detonate close to Ukrainian cargo planes.

French President Emmanuel Macron warned in September that the threat of hybrid attacks by Russia against Europe and France had intensified .
